answer.rationale: The p99 latency spike (5x target) correlates directly with a release 2 hours ago. During settlement peak with heavy writes, rollback is the fastest path to restore stability without data loss risk. memory_b1 confirms rollback cleared a similar checkout error spike cleanly on a stable prior build. memory_b2 warns against failover during hot writes—this constraint makes rollback safer than regional failover given current write intensity. memory_b3 shows the system has proven capacity headroom. Rollback isolates the recent code change as the root cause and restores the last known stable state in minutes, preserving all writes. This is lower-risk than circuit breaker (which still serves degraded) or capacity (which doesn't address the root cause of the spike). Read replica routing doesn't help write path latency.
